intro: When you search for event insurance near me, you are likely planning a wedding, conference, festival or other gathering and need cover for cancellation, public liability or equipment. You want to find a local insurance broker who understands events and can arrange the right policy for your situation. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK insurance broker who will quote you directly, with prices on application.
need_heading: What people arranging events usually need
need_lead: Event insurance is often required by venues and protects you against the unexpected.
needs: You have booked a venue that insists you have public liability cover before the event can go ahead.
You are organising a wedding and want cancellation cover in case illness or bad weather forces a change of plan.
You are running a conference and need to protect against financial loss if a key speaker cancels at short notice.
You own expensive sound or lighting equipment for a festival and want cover against damage or theft.
You are holding an outdoor event and need cover for abandonment due to extreme weather.
context_heading: Why you should arrange cover early
context: Many policies for event cancellation have conditions that must be met, such as taking out cover well before the event date. Buying early gives you the best chance of meeting those conditions and ensures you are covered if something unexpected happens.

Venues often require you to show proof of public liability insurance before they will confirm your booking. Without it, you may lose your deposit or be unable to proceed, so it is worth sorting cover as soon as your plans are firm.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us the type of event you are planning, such as a wedding, conference or festival, and the date and location.
Let us know how many people are expected to attend and whether the event is indoors or outdoors.
Mention any specific cover you need, such as cancellation, public liability or equipment protection.
Tell us if your venue has already asked for proof of insurance or specified a level of cover.
Let us know if you have any particular concerns, like adverse weather or supplier cancellation.
Tell us whether you have arranged event insurance before or if this is your first time.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the insurance broker
questions: Does this policy meet the requirements set by my venue?
What are the conditions for cancellation cover, and when must I take out the policy to be eligible?
Are there any exclusions for adverse weather or supplier failure that I should know about?
How much public liability cover does this policy provide, and is it enough for my event?
Does the policy cover my equipment if it is damaged or stolen during the event?
How and when will I receive my policy documents, and who do I contact if I need to make a claim?

faqs.q: Do I need event insurance if my venue already has insurance?
faqs.a: Yes, venues usually have their own insurance, but it does not cover your liabilities or losses. You will typically need your own public liability cover to protect against claims from attendees or damage you cause.

faqs.q: Can I get event insurance for a last-minute event?
faqs.a: Some policies can be arranged at short notice, but cancellation cover often has conditions about when you buy it. It is best to arrange cover as early as possible.

faqs.q: What does event insurance typically cover?
faqs.a: It can cover cancellation or abandonment, public liability, and equipment you own or hire. The exact cover depends on the policy, so check the details carefully.

faqs.q: How do I check that an insurance broker is authorised?
faqs.a: You can check on the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) register. Brokers must be authorised by the FCA or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm.
